topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It provides introductory framing and administrative context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Foundational Principles and Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the general architecture, naming conventions, and core biochemical mechanisms that center on complement component C3.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how distinct upstream recognition mechanisms detect pathogens and converge to trigger complement activation.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of the Complement Cascade
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the downstream actions activated by complement to destroy or mark pathogens for elimination.

topics.label: Host Regulation of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: It details the protective regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from causing damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Manifestations of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It describes the clinical presentations and disease patterns associated with deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Strategies Against Complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the mechanisms evolved by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to resist and evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: It delivers the closing framing remarks and previews the subject of the subsequent lecture.
